panel_intro: One question at a time — nothing here is submitted anywhere.

location.text: Is the vehicle currently stopped in a travel lane or another unsafe spot?

options.label: No, it's safely off the road

tire_type.text: Is this a run-flat tire, or do you have a spare?

confidence.text: Are you comfortable changing it yourself, safely off the road?

options.label: Yes, I can do it safely

unsafe_location.title: Move Only to Immediate Safety
unsafe_location.summary: Don't change a tire in a travel lane. If you can safely move a short distance — like onto the shoulder — do that first, then deal with the tire.
unsafe_location.confidence_text: A flat tire in an active lane is a real hazard regardless of how minor the tire damage looks.
not_to_do: Don't attempt to change the tire while in or near a travel lane.
Don't stand behind the vehicle in traffic to inspect it.
Don't drive further than the nearest safe shoulder.
before_help_checklist: Turn on hazard lights before and after moving.
Check mirrors and traffic before moving at all.
Once safely stopped, exit on the side away from traffic.
Call roadside assistance or a tow once you're safely off the road.

phone_script.intro: Read this once you're safely stopped and calling for help.
lines: Hi, I have a flat tire and I'm now safely stopped at [location description].
Can you confirm ETA, and whether you can swap in my spare or if I'll need a tow?

unsafe_location.next_action: Once you're safely off the road, use this tool again if anything about the situation has changed.

runflat_ok.title: Safe to Reassess
runflat_ok.summary: Run-flat tires are built to be driven a short distance at reduced speed (typically under 50 mph, up to about 50 miles) to reach a shop — but treat that as a limit, not a target.
runflat_ok.confidence_text: This depends on your specific tire's rated run-flat distance and speed, which this tool can't see.
not_to_do: Don't exceed the speed your tire and vehicle manual specify for run-flat driving.
Don't assume you can keep driving indefinitely — get it repaired or replaced promptly.
Don't ignore any handling changes; stop if the ride feels increasingly unstable.
before_help_checklist: Check your owner's manual for your specific run-flat speed and distance limit.
Turn on hazard lights if driving well below normal traffic speed.
Head directly to the nearest shop, not on a longer errand.
Have the tire inspected even if it seems to be holding up.

phone_script.intro: Worth calling ahead so the shop is ready for you.
lines: Hi, I have a run-flat tire that's damaged and I'm driving in carefully.
Can you take a look at it today?
Do you have this tire in stock, or will it need to be ordered?

runflat_ok.next_action: If the ride starts feeling unstable before you reach the shop, stop and call roadside assistance instead.

no_spare.title: Call Roadside Assistance First
no_spare.summary: No usable spare means a roadside tire service or tow is the practical next step.
no_spare.confidence_text: Without a spare, there's no safe DIY option — this is a straightforward roadside call.
not_to_do: Don't drive on the flat, even slowly — it can destroy the wheel.
Don't rely on a fix-a-flat can as anything more than a very short-term measure.
Don't assume every roadside plan carries your tire size — ask first.
before_help_checklist: Pull as far off the road as safely possible.
Turn on hazard lights.
Note your tire size if you can see it on the sidewall.
Stay on the side away from traffic while you wait.

phone_script.intro: Read this while you're on the phone with roadside assistance.
lines: Hi, I have a flat tire and no usable spare, at [location description].
Can you confirm ETA, and whether you carry tires or if I'll need a tow to a shop?

no_spare.next_action: Ask the shop to check why the spare wasn't usable, so you're covered next time.

diy_change.title: Safe to Reassess — You've Got This
diy_change.summary: Changing it yourself is reasonable if you're safely off the road with a proper spare and tools. Take your time and follow the order below.
diy_change.confidence_text: This assumes standard conditions — a firm, level surface and a spare in good condition. If anything feels off partway through, stop and call for help instead.
not_to_do: Don't work between the vehicle and moving traffic.
Don't rely on the jack alone — never put any body part under the vehicle.
Don't skip hand-tightening lug nuts in a star pattern before lowering the vehicle.
Don't drive far or fast on a compact spare — most are limited to around 50 mph.
before_help_checklist: Park on level, firm ground and set the parking brake.
Loosen (don't remove) the lug nuts before jacking up the vehicle.
Use the vehicle's jack points, not the plastic trim.
Tighten lug nuts fully once the vehicle is back on the ground, in a star pattern.

phone_script.intro: Keep this ready in case you need backup partway through.
lines: Hi, I'm changing a flat tire myself at [location description] but may need help.
Can you confirm ETA in case I call back?

diy_change.next_action: Get the flat repaired or replaced properly soon — don't treat the spare as permanent.

roadside_spare.title: Call Roadside Assistance First
roadside_spare.summary: You have a spare, but there's no shame in having a professional swap it in — especially if you're not confident doing it yourself.
roadside_spare.confidence_text: This is a textbook roadside-assistance case.
not_to_do: Don't attempt it if you're not confident, especially near traffic.
Don't drive on the flat while waiting — it can destroy the wheel.
Don't forget to mention you have a spare so they bring the right tools.
before_help_checklist: Pull as far off the road as safely possible.
Turn on hazard lights.
Have your spare and jack accessible for the technician.
Stay on the side away from traffic while you wait.

phone_script.intro: Read this while you're on the phone with roadside assistance.
lines: Hi, I have a flat tire and a spare, at [location description].
Can you confirm ETA for a tire swap?

roadside_spare.next_action: Get the flat repaired or replaced properly before driving on the spare long-term.
